ai.description: This large snake reaches 3 meters. It features a pale tan body with dark brown, rectangular blotches and a distinctive pinkish-brown "V" mark on the head. It has vestigial pelvic spurs near the vent.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Indian Rock Python is best distinguished by its dark, arrowhead-shaped head marking and the presence of light "eyes" within its dorsal blotches.
ai.habitat: The Indian Rock Python inhabits diverse environments, including tropical rainforests, scrublands, and marshes, typically ranging from sea level up to 2,000 meters in altitude.
ai.behavior: The Indian Rock Python is primarily nocturnal, using its heat-sensing labial pits to detect and ambush prey in the dark before constricting them.
ai.reproductionNotes: Indian Rock Pythons are oviparous, laying clutches of 15–100 eggs between March and June. Females brood their eggs to regulate temperature until they hatch.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Rock Python inhabits diverse biomes across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level to 2,000 meters in foothills, forests, and rocky scrublands.
